title: The Bright Colony
premise: When the children of Bright Colony begin dreaming identical memories of a massacre that never happened, insurance investigator Ulyana Winterbourne is hired to debunk the phenomenon before it shatters the fragile truce between the colony and the punitive fleet orbiting overhead. Digging through falsified manifests and sealed cargo holds, she discovers the dreams are real: a corporate purge erased an entire settlement's records, and its survivors' children carry the truth in their sleep. As the truce clock runs down, Ulyana must choose between broadcasting proof that will ignite war and burying it to keep the peace. She broadcasts it — but frames the evidence so the fleet's own tribunal, not mob justice, delivers the verdict, buying the colony survival at the cost of her license, her ship, and her clean record.
about_author: Rafael Eriksen is a former maritime claims adjuster who spent six years aboard research vessels in the North Atlantic before turning to fiction. He writes near-future thrillers about paperwork, conscience, and the people who read the fine print of history.

chapters.title: The Same Dream
chapters.summary: Ulyana arrives at Bright Colony on a routine fraud claim: forty children reporting one shared nightmare of fire and sealed doors. Told from Ulyana's skeptical POV, with interludes from ten-year-old Mira Kade, who dreams in another child's memories. The beat is unease — Ulyana expects hysteria or a hoax, but finds children who describe a docking bay that officially does not exist.

chapters.title: Paper Ashes
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV as she pulls cargo manifests and finds a decade of immaculate records too perfect to be true — every anomaly signed off by the same fleet auditor. When she interviews the auditor, he warns her off, then dies in an 'impossible' airlock accident that mirrors her old case files. The emotional beat shifts from professional curiosity to dread: someone is still editing reality, and she may be next.

chapters.title: What the Children Keep
chapters.summary: Alternating between Ulyana and Mira, this chapter reveals the source: survivors of the Halvard Station purge hid their trauma in an experimental memory-shield meant to protect the next generation, and it leaked instead. The fleet's truce expires in seventy-two hours; the colony council begs Ulyana to stay silent while hardliners prepare to seize the evidence by force. The beat is moral crisis — truth now has a body count attached to it.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV for the climax: she hijacks the fleet's own legal broadcast channel during the truce expiration ceremony, streaming the unsealed records and the children's corroborated testimony directly into the tribunal's jurisdiction, forcing a lawful trial no faction can veto without breaking the truce themselves. In the quiet aftermath, Mira thanks her; Ulyana, stripped of her license, watches the first honest record in ten years enter the archive. The beat is costly, hard-won justice.
